title: The Feasts of Israel
lead: The "set times" of the LORD (Leviticus 23:2) are Israel's weekly and yearly holy days: the Sabbath, Passover and Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, the day of trumpet blasts, the Day of Atonement and the Feast of Booths. Each has its own page; this page shows the calendar as a whole.

sections.b: Exodus names three pilgrimage feasts when all males appear before God: Unleavened Bread, Harvest (Weeks) and Ingathering (Booths) (Exodus 23:14–17; Exodus 34:18–24). Leviticus 23 gives the full calendar with dates; Numbers 28–29 lists the offerings; Deuteronomy 16 centers the feasts on the chosen place. Later books show them kept or restored (2 Chronicles 30; 2 Chronicles 35; Ezra 3:4; Nehemiah 8), and Purim (Esther 9) and Hanukkah (John 10:22) were added. Jesus goes up to the feasts in John's Gospel, and the Spirit comes at Pentecost (Acts 2:1). Paul calls the feasts "a shadow of the things to come" (Colossians 2:16–17).
